Subject: POC performance gates, stress metrics & next steps

Hi Sam / Ava —

Thanks again for a productive demo earlier. Per our call, I wanted to capture the performance-focused success criteria we discussed and the immediate next steps so we all have a single reference. High level ask from LuminarX: confirm that Redwood can meet the latency/throughput targets for your end-to-end pipeline and give a short stress validation plan.

Proposed POC success criteria (technical scope):
- Latency: median (p50) generation latency <= 120 ms; p95 <= 450 ms (measured at the model endpoint, end-to-end excludes client network)
- Throughput: sustained 75 req/s with 256-token average request length; ability to spike to 200 req/s for short bursts (1–2 minutes)
- Cost: target <= $0.12 / 1k tokens for the workload profile you shared (mix of short prompts + summarization)
- Quality: baseline evaluation set (attached) must maintain >= 92% of your current quality score on intent classification and entity extraction tests
- Stability: zero critical errors, <0.5% server errors during a 2-hour stress window

Attachments: I attached the sample_workload.csv you shared (as a starting point) and a short runbook we may use for the stress window.

Immediate next steps we proposed on the call:
1) Redwood: produce a short validation plan and confirm if the targets above are achievable with the model variant in the catalog (action: Karthik, due EOD Mon 6/14).
2) LuminarX: provide the production-ish sample file (anonymized) and S3 access or a signed URL for ingestion (action: Sam, due Wed 6/16).
3) Both: schedule a 90-minute POC kickoff for the week of 6/21 to run smoke tests and agree on measurement instrumentation (action: Grace to propose times).

If any of the metrics above don't match what you have in mind, call them out and we'll iterate. I included Karthik (solutions) and Ben (AE) on the thread for ops/contract sequencing.

Best,
Grace

- For cost, the $0.12/1k tokens is an important threshold for our CFO — can you confirm whether that assumes quantized weights and batching at 128 token windows?
- Security: our security team (security@luminarx.com) needs a short checklist and any SOC2 docs you have before we execute data transfer.

Hi all —

Short answer: feasible with the following notes and validation plan.

Assumptions / baseline
- Model: LlamaX-14B-opt (float16 w/ int8 quantization profile) — typical throughput/latency trade-offs apply.
- Batching: we will enable continuous batching with a soft batch target of 128 tokens and dynamic batch sizing based on request arrival.
- Hardware: Dedicated T4-like instance pool for baseline; can switch to A10/NVIDIA for lower p95 if needed.

Expected outcomes (approx):
- p50: ~90–110 ms (endpoint generation only)
- p95: ~300–420 ms (endpoint generation only)
- Sustained throughput: 80–90 req/s at 256-token average on a 3-node pool (T4-class); burst to 200 req/s achieved by temporary autoscale/burst capacity
- Cost: projected ~$0.09–0.13 / 1k tokens depending on average prompt length and batch efficiency (the $0.12 target is achievable with the quantized profile + tuning).

Validation plan (owner tags):
1) Prep (Karthik) — confirm the model variant and quantization profile to be used; load the provided sample_workload.csv and run a smoke harness to validate token distribution (due: Mon 6/14).
2) Instrumentation (Karthik & LuminarX) — we will publish endpoint metrics (p50/p95, cpu/gpu utilization, batch sizes) to the shared metrics endpoint; LuminarX to deploy a client tracer to capture end-to-end times (due: before kickoff).
3) Stress window (Karthik) — 2-hour controlled run: step 1 ramp to sustained 75 req/s for 90 minutes; step 2 3x burst tests (2 min each) to 200 req/s; record errors, retry rates, and latency distributions. We'll run with the quantized profile and record cost per 1k tokens during the run (date: scheduled during kickoff week).
4) Analysis & readout (Karthik, Grace) — produce a short readout doc with latency histograms, throughput graphs, cost calculations, and any regressions in quality relative to the baseline eval set (deliverable: 24 hours after run).

Caveats:
- If LuminarX's end-to-end network latency is high, p95 numbers will diverge from endpoint-only metrics; we'll provide both.
- Extreme variance in input length will reduce batching efficiency and push cost/latency up; sample distribution is important.

Attachments: I attached a short runbook (runbook_stress_test.md) and an example sample_workload.csv for the smoke harness.

If this plan looks good I can draft a short MIP (measurement/instrumentation plan) and a calendar invite for the kickoff.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
